author: claude
desc: Find the exact reason m1n1's minilzlib XzDecode returns false on large -9e-compressed real initramfs. Established in 160: reproduces on the host harness (scripts/t6040-minilzlib-harness.sh); NOT a simple size limit (200 MiB zeros and 200 MiB real -6 both decode; 192 MiB real -9e decodes; 278 MiB real -9e fails), so it tracks compressed structure at -9e's 64 MiB dictionary, not uncompressed size. RULED OUT earlier: XZ block-header size metadata (flags 0x0000), dict-size property (checked only for >39 log2). CANDIDATES: (a) Lz2DecodeStream chunk loop returning false after N chunks; (b) the XzDecodeIndex VLI meta-check (MINLZ_META_CHECKS is defined) comparing UnpaddedBlockSize/UncompressedBlockSize where a VLI or accumulator is too narrow; (c) a uint32 wrap in a compressed-offset accumulator (input is ~67 MiB, within uint32, but intermediate products may not be). METHOD, all offline with the harness: instrument XzDecode/Lz2DecodeStream to print which check fails and at what chunk/offset, then bisect -9e real content to the exact crossover. If it is a genuine minilzlib bug, a minimal upstream-shaped fix in ~/Code/m1n1 would raise the real ceiling; if it is a spec limit, document it. Low priority — 128 MiB guard + harness already keep us safe. Evidence: done/2026-07-27-t6040-minilzlib-decode-limit-harness.md.
